item.title: Moral Distress, Burnout, and the Intensive Care Unit Environment.
item.description: This article examines the relationship between moral distress and burnout among intensive care unit (ICU) clinicians and argues that moral distress acts as a precursor to burnout. item.description: Hypernatremia is frequent in the intensive care unit (ICU) and is associated with adverse outcomes. We investigated global treatment preferences and clinicians' willingness to enroll patients in a randomized trial to inform its feasibility. item.description: Sepsis is a major global health challenge and increasingly affects patients with complex conditions such as malignancy. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to clarify endpoint-specific prognostic associations between malignancy and mortality in adults with sepsis or septic shock. item.description: This study looked at Japanese physiotherapists who worked with COVID-19 patients and found that direct contact with patients contributed to burnout, but this effect was partly buffered by appreciation and respect from patients and colleagues.
